items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I remember one time, we were playing 'After You're Gone,' and we were playing it like Roy did with Krupa... he snatched his horn down... I said, 'Well, that's right, you're not. You're not gonna play another note. You're through.'

ctx.x: So there were a lot of guys in Chicago just waiting for guys to goof, you know, and I only had one. There was a little guy named Hubert Dodson. He didn't become famous, but he was in that era along with Gene Ammonds, he came along with -- but he was an excellent reader, and he could play first, second, or third trumpet. He played beautifully, but he was weird, man, upstairs, you know. I remember one time, he was playing a solo, and he idolized Roy Eldridge, and he could play and he had good chops. And I remember…

showing up on the job, getting drunk, or one of those things like -- I don't know. The guys wanted to play, I think, in those days, you know. They took it serious. It was a little bit different in my brother's band in that way, of course. But the guys knew how to hold their drinks. I shouldn't even say that. They knew how to hold the drinks. But playing in places like the Roseland on Broadway, you don't goof up jobs like that. So, I don't know if that answers your question or not, but the drinking thing didn't…
